findings.title: Federated rules are no longer treated as immutable by combined-rule ability checks
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which unconditionally sets `isFederated` to `false`. The previous combined-rule implementation inspected `rule.group.source_tenants` via `isFederatedRuleGroup`, so callers of `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` can now receive supported edit, delete, pause, restore, and permanent-delete abilities for federated rule groups. Federated rules must remain non-editable; retain the group federation check when adapting the combined-rule path.

findings.title: Pause and delete actions are suppressed for prom-only Grafana list items
findings.body: The new Grafana list passes only `promRule`, so the Grafana-prom ability checks can authorize pause and delete, but the menu still renders Pause only when a `rulerRule` is present (line 123) and Delete only when a `rulerRule` is present (line 165). Consequently, authorized users cannot pause or delete any Grafana-managed rule from the list after the ruler fetch is removed. These actions need a prom-rule-compatible implementation or must be handled by identifier rather than being gated on the absent ruler DTO.

findings.title: Silence menu items in the prom-only list are visible but do nothing
findings.body: For a `GrafanaRuleListItem`, `RuleActionsButtons` receives no `rule`/ruler DTO. `AlertRuleMenu` can still show “Silence notifications” from the new prom-rule ability and its handler sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but this component renders `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true. With `rule` undefined the condition is always false, leaving the visible menu action as a no-op. Pass a supported prom-rule representation to the drawer or do not expose the action until it can be performed.

findings.title: Grafana recording rules lose the existing modify-export capability
findings.body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` uses `isAlertingRule` as the support condition for `ModifyExport`. That predicate excludes Grafana-managed recording rules, so the direct prom-only list will not show Export for those rules even for users with export permission. The prior ruler-based ability used the generic Grafana-rule predicate, which included both alerting and recording rules. Use the generic Grafana rule check for this capability unless recording-rule export is intentionally being removed and the route is changed accordingly.

findings.title: Rule detail links no longer preserve the originating list URL
findings.body: The previous Grafana list item built its view URL with `createReturnTo()` and supplied it as the `returnTo` query parameter. This replacement builds `/alerting/grafana/<uid>/view` without it, so opening a rule from a filtered/list view loses the return target used by the detail/edit flow and sends users back to the default alerting page rather than their current list context. Preserve the existing `returnTo` parameter when creating this link.

findings.title: Grafana entries in filtered results are returned without the computed React key
findings.body: `FilterViewResults` computes a unique `key` specifically for list identity, but the Grafana branch returns `GrafanaRuleListItem` without passing that key. Any filtered result containing multiple Grafana rules produces React's missing-key warning, and React cannot reliably retain item-local state if the result set is reconciled. Pass `key={key}` as is already done for datasource and unknown-rule branches.

findings.title: GrafanaGroupLoader documentation still claims it loads the Ruler endpoint
findings.body: The component now only calls `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery`, but its documentation says it loads both Prometheus and Ruler endpoints. The `expectedRulesCount` documentation also refers to a Ruler response. Update these comments so future changes do not assume a ruler request or ruler/prometheus reconciliation still exists.
